claim: An animal entering a new environment typically faces three challenges: explore the space for resources, memorize their locations, and navigate towards those targets as needed.
source: An animal entering a new environment typically faces three challenges: explore the space for resources, memorize their locations, and navigate towards those targets as needed.
evidence: This is a general statement about animal behavior that draws from established understanding in behavioral ecology and neuroscience.

claim: The endotaxis algorithm can be implemented with a simple 3-layer neural circuit using only biologically realistic structures and learning rules.
source: This endotaxis algorithm can be implemented with a simple 3-layer neural circuit using only biologically realistic structures and learning rules.
evidence: This claim is supported by the detailed circuit model presented in Figure 1B and the mathematical formulations throughout the manuscript.

claim: Several neural components of the endotaxis scheme are found in brains from insects to humans.
source: Several neural components of this scheme are found in brains from insects to humans.
evidence: This is supported by the Discussion section which references specific brain structures like the mushroom body in insects and hippocampus in mammals.

claim: Chemotaxis is common to all animals.
source: One algorithm for finding a valuable resource is common to all animals: chemotaxis. Every motile species has a way to track odors through the environment, either to find the source of the odor or to avoid it (Baker et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Baker et al., 2018.

claim: Brains originally evolved to organize the motor response in pursuit of chemical stimuli.
source: It is believed that brains originally evolved to organize the motor response in pursuit of chemical stimuli.
evidence: This is presented as a belief in the field, indicating it draws from established scientific consensus.

claim: Some of the oldest regions of the mammalian brain, including the hippocampus, seem organized around an axis that processes smells.
source: Indeed, some of the oldest regions of the mammalian brain, including the hippocampus, seem organized around an axis that processes smells (Jacobs, 2012; Aboitiz and Montiel, 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Jacobs, 2012 and Aboitiz and Montiel, 2015.

claim: The toolkit for chemotaxis always includes a search strategy based on trial-and-error.
source: The specifics of chemotaxis, namely the methods for finding an odor and tracking it, vary by species, but the toolkit always includes a search strategy based on trial-and-error: try various actions that you have available, then settle on the one that makes the odor stronger (Baker et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Baker et al., 2018.

claim: Mice can navigate back out of a labyrinth using a direct route they had not traveled before, even on the first attempt.
source: Furthermore, they could navigate back out of the labyrinth using a direct route they had not traveled before, even on the first attempt.
evidence: This is an observation from the experimental study by Rosenberg et al., 2021.

claim: Mice spent most of their waking time patrolling the labyrinth, even long after they had perfected the routes to rewarding locations.
source: Finally, the animals spent most of their waking time patrolling the labyrinth, even long after they had perfected the routes to rewarding locations.
evidence: This is an observation from the experimental study by Rosenberg et al., 2021.

claim: The endotaxis circuit includes four types of neurons: resource cells, point cells, map cells, and goal cells.
source: The model includes four types of neurons: resource cells, point cells, map cells, and goal cells.
evidence: This is explicitly stated in the text and shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Resource cells are sensory neurons that fire when the animal encounters an interesting resource.
source: These are sensory neurons that fire when the animal encounters an interesting resource, for example, water or food, that may form a target for future navigation.
evidence: This is a definition provided in the model description.

claim: Point cells represent the animal's location with small receptive fields localized in the environment.
source: Each neuron in this population has a small response field within the environment. The neuron fires when the animal enters that response field.
evidence: This is a definition provided in the model description.

claim: Point cells exist from the outset as soon as the animal enters the environment.
source: We assume that these point cells exist from the outset as soon as the animal enters the environment.
evidence: This is an explicit assumption of the model.

claim: Map cells learn the structure of the environment through modifiable recurrent synapses.
source: This layer of neurons learns the structure of the environment, namely how the various locations are connected in space. The map cells get excitatory input from point cells in a one-to-one fashion. These input synapses are static. The map cells also excite each other with all-to-all connections. These recurrent synapses are modifiable according to a local plasticity rule.
evidence: This is a description of the model architecture and learning mechanism.

claim: After learning, the map synapses represent the topology of the environment.
source: After learning, they represent the topology of the environment.
evidence: This is a claim about the outcome of the learning process in the model.

claim: Goal cells mark the locations of special resources in the map of the environment.
source: Each goal cell serves to mark the locations of a special resource in the map of the environment.
evidence: This is a description of the function of goal cells in the model.

claim: The output of the goal cell declines systematically with the distance of the animal from the target location.
source: The key insight is that the output of the goal cell declines systematically with the distance of the animal from the target location.
evidence: This is a key theoretical result demonstrated mathematically and through simulations.

claim: When the animal moves from one location to an adjacent one, the synapses between the two corresponding map cells undergo Hebbian strengthening.
source: When the animal moves from one location to an adjacent one, those two point cells fire in rapid succession. That leads to a Hebbian strengthening of the excitatory synapses between the two corresponding map cells (Figure 2A and B).
evidence: This describes the learning rule for map synapses, illustrated in Figure 2.

claim: The matrix of synaptic connections among map cells converges to the correlation matrix of their inputs, which reflects the adjacency matrix of the graph.
source: To a first approximation, the matrix of synaptic connections among the map cells will converge to the correlation matrix of their inputs (Dayan and Abbott, 2001; Galtier et al., 2012), which in turn reflects the adjacency matrix of the graph (Equation 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Dayan and Abbott, 2001 and Galtier et al., 2012, and by the mathematical formulation.

claim: At a noise level of ε=0.01, navigation is perfect over distances of ~9 steps, independent of the nature of the graph.
source: With a noise level of 1%, the resulting goal signal allows perfect navigation over distances of ∼9 steps, independent of the nature of the graph.
evidence: This is a result from simulations on multiple graph types shown in Figure 5.

claim: The required tuning of endotaxis parameters is rather generous, allowing at least 10–20% slop in the parameters for reasonable performance.
source: At the same time, the required tuning is rather generous, allowing at least 10–20% slop in the parameters for reasonable performance.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the parameter sensitivity analysis shown in Figure 6.

claim: The saturating activation function allowed for higher gain values, which led to considerable increases in the range of navigation.
source: However, the saturating activation function allowed for higher gain values, which led to considerable increases in the range of navigation: by a factor of 2.2 for the ring graph, and 1.5 for the Tower of Hanoi graph.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from simulations shown in Figure 7.

claim: Mice can return to the entrance from inside a labyrinth using the shortest path without error on the very first visit.
source: Experimentally we found that mice indeed take the short direct route instead of retracing their path (Rosenberg et al., 2021). They can do so even on the very first visit of an unfamiliar labyrinth.
evidence: This is an experimental observation from Rosenberg et al., 2021.

claim: Endotaxis can explain the homing behavior observed in mice navigating a labyrinth for the first time.
source: Can endotaxis explain this behavior?
evidence: This is demonstrated through simulations shown in Figure 8.

claim: In the binary tree maze, the optimal patrol path takes 252 steps and visits every end node exactly once without any repeats.
source: In the binary tree maze used for our experiments, that optimal patrol path takes 252 steps: it visits every end node of the labyrinth exactly once without any repeats (Figure 9A).
evidence: This is a computational result shown in Figure 9A.

claim: Real mice patrolling behavior is much more efficient than random but not quite optimal.
source: Real mice do not quite execute this optimal path, but their patrolling behavior is much more efficient than random (Figure 9B).
evidence: This is based on experimental data from Rosenberg et al., 2021, shown in Figure 9B.

claim: The mushroom body of the arthropod brain contains neural circuit elements similar to those proposed in the endotaxis model.
source: A prominent instance of this motif is found in the mushroom body of the arthropod brain (Heisenberg, 2003; Strausfeld et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Heisenberg, 2003 and Strausfeld et al., 2009.

claim: Kenyon cells in the mushroom body have sparse odor responses.
source: Here the Kenyon cells, with their sparse odor responses (Stopfer, 2014), play the role of both point and map cells.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Stopfer, 2014.

claim: Most of the Kenyon cell output synapses are onto other Kenyon cells.
source: They are strongly recurrently connected; in fact, most of the Kenyon cell output synapses are onto other Kenyon cells (Eichler et al., 2017; Takemura et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Eichler et al., 2017 and Takemura et al., 2017.

claim: Plasticity at the synapse between Kenyon cells and mushroom body output neurons is gated by neuromodulators that encode rewards or punishments.
source: Plasticity at the synapse between Kenyon cells and output neurons is gated by neuromodulators that encode rewards or punishments (Cohn et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Cohn et al., 2015.

claim: Mushroom body output neurons are known to guide the turning decisions of insects.
source: Mushroom body output neurons are known to guide the turning decisions of the insect (Aso et al., 2014), perhaps through their projections to the central complex (Li et al., 2020), an area critical to the animal's turning behavior (Honkanen et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Aso et al., 2014, Li et al., 2020, and Honkanen et al., 2019.

claim: Insects can use odors as landmarks in the environment for navigation.
source: But the endotaxis model suggests a different interpretation: insects can also use odors as landmarks in the environment. In this more general form of navigation, the odor is not a goal in itself, but serves to mark a route toward some entirely different goal (Knaden and Graham, 2016; Steck et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Knaden and Graham, 2016 and Steck et al., 2009.

claim: Many place cells in the rodent hippocampus appear within minutes of the animal's entry into an arena.
source: Indeed, many place cells in the rodent hippocampus appear within minutes of the animal's entry into an arena (Wilson and McNaughton, 1993; Frank et al., 2004).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Wilson and McNaughton, 1993 and Frank et al., 2004.

claim: Any given environment activates only a small fraction of potential place cells in the hippocampus.
source: Furthermore, any given environment activates only a small fraction of these neurons. Most of the 'potential place cells' remain silent, presumably because their sensory trigger feature does not match any of the locations in the current environment (Alme et al., 2014; Epsztein et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Alme et al., 2014 and Epsztein et al., 2011.

claim: Goal cells with large place fields centered on a goal location have been reported in rat cortex.
source: Indeed, such cells have been reported in rat cortex (Hok et al., 2005).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Hok et al., 2005.

claim: A hippocampal neuron can suddenly start firing with a fully formed place field that may be located anywhere in the environment.
source: This prediction is reminiscent of a startling experimental observation in recordings from hippocampal area CA1: a neuron can suddenly start firing with a fully formed place field that may be located anywhere in the environment (Bittner et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Bittner et al., 2017.

claim: The sudden appearance of place fields is triggered by a calcium plateau potential in the dendrites of the place cell, which potentiates the excitatory synaptic inputs.
source: This event appears to be triggered by a calcium plateau potential in the dendrites of the place cell, which potentiates the excitatory synaptic inputs the cell receives.
evidence: This is based on experimental observations referenced in the context of Bittner et al., 2017.

claim: There is a plasticity mechanism in hippocampal neurons that extends over several seconds.
source: Subsequent cellular measurements indeed revealed a plasticity mechanism that extends over several seconds (Magee and Grienberger, 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Magee and Grienberger, 2020.

claim: Endotaxis represents a brain module that could be interposed between a spatial-sensing module and a taxis module.
source: Effectively, endotaxis represents a brain module that could be interposed between a spatial-sensing module, which produces place cells, and a taxis module, which delivers the movements to ascend a goal signal.
evidence: This is a conceptual claim about how endotaxis fits into brain architecture.

claim: Animals navigate by real-world trial-and-error, at least in the early phase of learning.
source: In fact, there is strong evidence that animals navigate by real-world trial-and-error, at least in the early phase of learning (Redish, 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Redish, 2016.

claim: Rats at a decision point often hesitate with a swaying back and forth between passages, called 'vicarious trial and error'.
source: Lashley, 1912, in his first scientific paper on visual discrimination in the rat, reported that rats at a decision point often hesitate 'with a swaying back and forth between the passages.'
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Lashley, 1912.

claim: Similar vicarious trial and error behaviors occur in arthropods and humans when poised at a decision point.
source: Similar behaviors occur in arthropods (Tarsitano, 2006) and humans (Santos-Pata and Verschure, 2018) when poised at a decision point.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Tarsitano, 2006 and Santos-Pata and Verschure, 2018.

claim: The shortest route can be navigated one step at a time without any high-level advanced planning.
source: Thus, the shortest route can be navigated one step at a time without any high-level advanced planning. This is the core idea behind endotaxis.
evidence: This is a key conceptual claim about how endotaxis works.

claim: The network of map cells effectively computes the shortest graph distances.
source: The network of Figure 1B effectively computes the shortest graph distances.
evidence: This is demonstrated through mathematical derivations and simulations.

claim: An agent that makes local turning decisions to maximize the goal signal will reach the goal by the shortest possible path.
source: Therefore, an agent that makes local turning decisions to maximize that goal signal will reach the goal by the shortest possible path.
evidence: This is a theoretical result derived from the mathematical analysis.

claim: The exponential decay of the goal signal represents a challenge for practical implementation with biological circuits due to finite signal-to-noise ratio.
source: The exponential decay of the goal signal represents a challenge for practical implementation with biological circuits. Neurons have a finite signal-to-noise ratio, so detecting minute differences in the firing rate of a goal neuron will be unreliable.
evidence: This is an inference about biological constraints based on known properties of neurons.

claim: Humans and animals can routinely discriminate sensory stimuli that differ by only 1%.
source: For reference, humans and animals can routinely discriminate sensory stimuli that differ by only 1%, for example, the pitch of tones or the intensity of a light, especially if they occur in close succession.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge in psychophysics.

claim: An agent performing a random walk would take about 40 times longer to reach the target than by using endotaxis on the ring graph.
source: By contrast, an agent performing a random walk with zero knowledge of the environment would take about 40 times longer to reach the target than by using endotaxis (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is a quantitative comparison from simulations shown in Figure 5C.

claim: Endotaxis shortens the time to target by a factor of 100 on the binary tree graph.
source: Finally, comparison with the random agent shows that endotaxis shortens the time to target by a factor of 100 on this graph (Figure 5F).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from simulations shown in Figure 5F.

claim: Endotaxis speeds up the solution of the Tower of Hanoi game by a factor of 10 compared to random moves.
source: However, compared to an agent executing random moves, endotaxis speeds up the solution by a factor of 10 (Figure 5I).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from simulations shown in Figure 5I.

claim: Endotaxis functions well in environments with very different structure: linear, tree-shaped, and cyclic.
source: These results show that endotaxis functions well in environments with very different structure: linear, tree-shaped, and cyclic.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from simulations on multiple graph types shown in Figure 5.

claim: Personal experience suggests that we rarely learn routes that involve more than nine successive decisions.
source: This is a respectable range: personal experience suggests that we rarely learn routes that involve more than nine successive decisions.
evidence: This is an informal observation based on common experience.

claim: Chess openings, which are often played in a fast and reflexive fashion, last about 10 moves.
source: Chess openings, which are often played in a fast and reflexive fashion, last about 10 moves.
evidence: This is a factual statement about chess that is common knowledge.

claim: The saturating activation function keeps the peak output of the map constant, which has a normalizing effect.
source: Both these aspects of enhanced performance can be traced to the normalizing effect of the nonlinearity that keeps the peak output of the map constant.
evidence: This is an explanation for why the saturating activation function improves performance.

claim: The agent does not retrace its steps when arriving at location (2) during homing, but instead turns toward (1).
source: Note specifically that the agent does not retrace its steps when arriving at location (2), but instead turns toward (1).
evidence: This is an observation from the homing simulation shown in Figure 8.

claim: In the mouse study, animals spent more than 85% of the time patrolling the maze.
source: In our study of mice freely interacting with a large labyrinth, the animals spent more than 85% of the time patrolling the maze (Rosenberg et al., 2021).
evidence: This is an experimental observation from Rosenberg et al., 2021.

claim: Mice continued patrolling for hours after they had perfected the targeting of reward locations and homing back to the entrance.
source: This continued for hours after they had perfected the targeting of reward locations and the homing back to the entrance.
evidence: This is an experimental observation from Rosenberg et al., 2021.

claim: Endotaxis is 'always on' and does not require separating the phase of spatial learning from goal-directed navigation.
source: By contrast, endotaxis is 'always on.' Whether the animal explores a new environment, navigates to a target, or patrols a well-known graph, the synaptic learning rules are always the same.
evidence: This is a distinguishing feature of the endotaxis model compared to other models.

claim: Endotaxis can get an animal from zero knowledge to a cognitive map that allows reliable navigation toward goals discovered on a previous foray.
source: Endotaxis can get an animal from zero knowledge to a cognitive map that allows reliable navigation toward goals discovered on a previous foray.
evidence: This is a summary claim about the capabilities of endotaxis demonstrated through simulations.

claim: Endotaxis does not implement more advanced routines of spatial reasoning, such as stringing a habitual sequence of actions together or deliberating internally to plan entire routes.
source: But it does not implement more advanced routines of spatial reasoning, such as stringing a habitual sequence of actions together into one, or deliberating internally to plan entire routes.
evidence: This is an explicit limitation of the endotaxis model.

claim: A key characteristic of endotaxis is the reliance on trial-and-error, distinct from other forms of navigation.
source: A key characteristic of endotaxis, distinct from other forms of navigation, is the reliance on trial-and-error.
evidence: This is a conceptual claim about the nature of endotaxis.

claim: The agent does not deliberate to plan the shortest path to the goal in endotaxis.
source: The agent does not deliberate to plan the shortest path to the goal.
evidence: This is a description of how endotaxis operates.

claim: Endotaxis can be seen as a form of reinforcement learning where the agent learns from rewards or punishments in the environment.
source: Broadly speaking, endotaxis can be seen as a form of reinforcement learning (Sutton and Barto, 2018): the agent learns from rewards or punishments in the environment and develops a policy that allows for subsequent navigation to special locations.
evidence: This is a conceptual comparison to reinforcement learning theory, supported by a citation.

claim: The agent learns how to navigate to the goal location from a single reinforcement in endotaxis.
source: Thus, the agent learns how to navigate to the goal location from a single reinforcement (Figure 4).
evidence: This is demonstrated in simulations shown in Figure 4.

claim: In animal behavior, the acquisition of a cognitive map without rewards is called latent learning.
source: In animal behavior, the acquisition of a cognitive map without rewards is called latent learning.
evidence: This is a definition from the field of animal behavior.

claim: Early debates in animal psychology pitched latent learning and reinforcement learning as alternative explanations.
source: Early debates in animal psychology pitched latent learning and reinforcement learning as alternative explanations (Thistlethwaite, 1951).
evidence: This is a historical claim supported by a citation to Thistlethwaite, 1951.

claim: In endotaxis, neither latent learning nor reinforcement learning can function without the other as the goal signal explicitly depends on both the map and goal synapses.
source: Instead, in the endotaxis algorithm, neither can function without the other as the goal signal explicitly depends on both the map and goal synapses (Equation 18, Algorithm 1).
evidence: This is a conceptual claim about how endotaxis integrates both types of learning.

claim: The neural signals in endotaxis bear some similarity to the successor representation.
source: More specifically, the neural signals in endotaxis bear some similarity to the so-called successor representation (Dayan, 1993; Corneil and Gerstner, 2015; Stachenfeld et al., 2017; Garvert et al., 2017; Fang et al., 2023).
evidence: This is a comparison to another theoretical framework, supported by multiple citations.

claim: In endotaxis, there is no time/reward tradeoff and the agent simply wants the shortest path to the goal.
source: In endotaxis, there is no time/reward tradeoff. The agent simply wants the shortest path to the goal.
evidence: This is a conceptual distinction between endotaxis and the successor representation.

claim: Endotaxis does not tabulate the list of available actions at each state; that information remains externalized in the environment.
source: Second, endotaxis does not tabulate the list of available actions at each state. That information remains externalized in the environment: the agent simply tries whatever actions are available at the moment, then picks the best one.
evidence: This is a distinguishing feature of endotaxis compared to other reinforcement learning algorithms.

claim: For any given navigation policy in endotaxis, the agent needs to learn only one scalar function of location, namely the goal signal.
source: This 'externalized cognition' simplifies the learning task: for any given navigation policy, the agent needs to learn only one scalar function of location, namely the goal signal.
evidence: This is an explanation of the computational simplicity of endotaxis.

claim: Many machine learning algorithms develop a value function for state–action pairs, which allows more sophisticated planning.
source: By comparison, many machine learning algorithms develop a value function for state–action pairs, which then allows more sophisticated planning (Sutton and Barto, 2018; Moerland et al., 2023).
evidence: This is a comparison to other machine learning approaches, supported by citations.

claim: The relative simplicity of the endotaxis circuit depends on the limitation to learning only state functions.
source: The relative simplicity of the endotaxis circuit depends on the limitation to learning only state functions.
evidence: This is an explanation of a tradeoff in the endotaxis model.

claim: Several models assume the existence of a map layer where individual neurons stand for specific places and excitatory synapses represent connections between those places.
source: Several models assume the existence of a map layer, in which individual neurons stand for specific places, and the excitatory synapses between neurons represent the connections between those places (Gaussier et al., 2002; Schölkopf and Mallot, 1995; Voicu and Schmajuk, 2000; Trullier and Meyer, 2000; Martinet et al., 2011; Ponulak and Hopfield, 2013; Khajeh-Alijani et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a review of prior work, supported by multiple citations.

claim: The most popular scheme for reading out the map is to inject a signal into the desired end node, let it propagate backward through the network, and read out the magnitude or gradient near the start node.
source: The most popular scheme is to somehow inject a signal into the desired end node, let it propagate backward through the network, and read out the magnitude or gradient of the signal near the start node (Glasius et al., 1996; Gaussier et al., 2002; Gorchetchnikov and Hasselmo, 2005; Martinet et al., 2011; Ponulak and Hopfield, 2013; Khajeh-Alijani et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a review of prior work, supported by multiple citations.

claim: In endotaxis, the signal is propagated in the forward direction starting with the activity of the place cell at the agent's current location.
source: By contrast, in the endotaxis model the signal is propagated in the forward direction starting with the activity of the place cell at the agent's current location.
evidence: This is a distinguishing feature of endotaxis compared to other models.

claim: In endotaxis, the goal neuron is the same neuron that also responds directly to the rewarding feature at the goal location.
source: The signal strength is read out at the goal location: The goal neuron is the same neuron that also responds directly to the rewarding feature at the goal location.
evidence: This is a key feature of the endotaxis architecture.

claim: Many navigation models have to separate the phase of spatial learning from the phase of goal-directed navigation.
source: Another distinguishing feature of endotaxis is that it operates continuously. Many models for navigation have to separate the phase of spatial learning from the phase of goal-directed navigation.
evidence: This is a comparison to other models in the literature.

claim: In some navigation models, plasticity needs to be turned off or reset during one phase or the other.
source: Sometimes plasticity needs to be turned off or reset during one phase or the other (Samsonovich and Ascoli, 2005; Ponulak and Hopfield, 2013).
evidence: This is a review of limitations in prior models, supported by citations.

claim: Various components of the endotaxis model have appeared in other proposed schemes for spatial learning and navigation.
source: In summary, various components of the endotaxis model have appeared in other proposed schemes for spatial learning and navigation.
evidence: This is a summary statement about the relationship of endotaxis to prior work.

claim: The endotaxis model stands out in that all essential functions are covered in a feed-forward and neuromorphically plausible manner.
source: The present model stands out in that all the essential functions are covered in a feed-forward and neuromorphically plausible manner, without invoking unexplained control schemes.
evidence: This is a claim about the distinguishing features of endotaxis compared to other models.
